transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (VP ML, Northwood), Ethan Cole (Platform Eng), Sofia Alvarez (SRE), Kenji Ito (Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick Q2 operational readiness / coverage check focused on adoption patterns, cost drivers, and reliability runoff. Action: Redwood to provide granular cost heatmap and batching recommendations; Northwood to run a staging benchmark on Dedicated. Planned security deep-dive next week.

Topics Covered:
- Current usage and token distribution
- Cost hotspots (embeddings vs generation, long context jobs)
- Tail latency incidents and mitigation (KV cache, batching)
- Rollout coverage: hosted fallback & Dedicated sizing
- Security & compliance next steps (KMS, audit logs, SSO)

Action items (captured in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, i'll kick us off. quick agenda — usage, costs, reliability, then next steps. sound good?
[00:16] Priya Rao: yeah that works for us. quick note, we have two folks in the background but main people listed.
[00:22] Jon Park: hi team, jon from redwood infra, i'll cover batching/caching recommendations and one-off latency things.
[00:28] Ethan Cole: hey, ethan here. we hit a couple of high tail latency spikes last week during the nightly scoring job — want to understand trade offs if we move more to dedicated.
[00:38] Ava Martinez: noted, and congrats on ramping usage — you are up ~2.7x month over month, correct priya?
[00:44] Priya Rao: yeah up a lot, the recommender feature shipped in late april so that's the main driver. embeddings volume is also increasing because experiments for personalization are running nightly.
[00:55] Jon Park: can you share the token breakdown? embedding v. gen vs average sequence length, that drives different kernel choices and batching.
[01:05] Priya Rao: sure i posted the rough numbers in the thread — avg generation is ~150 tokens, embeddings 512 dims per request but small batch sizes now.
[01:14] Jon Park: okay so two obvious cost hotspots: small embedding requests (lots of tiny calls) and the long generation tails. batching helps embeddings massively; prefix caching helps the gens if prompts share prefixes.
[01:26] Ethan Cole: when you say prefix caching do you mean the kv cache? we've seen cache thrashing when we spin up new replicas.
[01:34] Jon Park: right, KV cache — we sometimes see poor locality if autoscale creates many cold workers. two levers: keep a steady baseline of Dedicated capacity and use sticky routing; and enable small cold-start warmers.
[01:47] Priya Rao: hmmm sticky routing is fine but we worry about cost if we hold a baseline. what's the sweet spot?
[01:53] Ava Martinez: that's why we'll send scenarios — baseline sizing with burst, and a pure-hosted fallback plan. you can see the economics side-by-side.
[02:02] Kenji Ito: question on fallback — if dedicated is out of capacity and we route to hosted do we lose audit log continuity? our compliance team asked.
[02:12] Jon Park: good question — current behavior depends on deployment: for Redwood Dedicated we replicate audit logs back to your customer org (configurable). if you fallback to hosted we'll still provide request-level logs but they appear in the hosted plane and there's a note about residency. short answer: logs exist but the storage location can differ; we can lock down retention and export to your KMS-backed storage.
[02:36] Sofia Alvarez: can we get that documented? also KMS key rotation policy — SOC team wants explicit flow.
[02:42] Ava Martinez: yep security deep-dive next week. we'll bring our SecOps and get KMS/HSM and audit log flows mapped.
[02:49] Priya Rao: ok good. back to the reliability we saw spikes — they correlate with nightly batch scoring. is the recommendation to move those jobs to a Dedicated pool?
[02:58] Jon Park: possible approaches: 1) move heavy nightly scoring to a Dedicated reserved pool sized for the peak, 2) keep jobs in hosted but use scheduled capacity reservations (if available), 3) rework scoring to smaller micro-batches with caching. each has cost/complexity tradeoffs.
[03:15] Ethan Cole: do you have a quick ballpark difference? we want to know monthly delta.
[03:20] Ava Martinez: we'll include scenario numbers — rough rule of thumb: if you have sustained heavy nightly loads (multi-hour, thousands of requests) Dedicated often becomes cheaper when you amortize GPUs; if it's bursty and unpredictable, hosted may be cheaper but with higher tail latency risk.
[03:36] Priya Rao: our current SLA target for recommender is p95 < 400ms interactive. we've been at p95 ~ 520ms during peak.
[03:46] Jon Park: 520ms p95 — do you have the token-level latency? often long tail is due to long-context generation or memory thrash. can you paste a sample trace?
[03:54] Priya Rao: i'll send a trace after this call.
[03:57] Jon Park: thanks. meanwhile for immediate mitigation: increase batch size for embeddings (reduce per-call overhead), enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, and consider short lived warm pools during the nightly window.
[04:09] Ethan Cole: for embeddings — is it trivial to change on our side? we have many microservices calling the embeddings endpoint independently.
[04:16] Jon Park: there are two paths: change client to aggregate micro-batches (best long term), or use a lightweight proxy that batches for you (quick win). we can supply an example lambda/proxy pattern.
[04:27] Ava Martinez: jon will attach a sample proxy and some client snippets.
[04:31] Kenji Ito: how do these changes affect result latency? if we batch embeddings we increase time to first byte for an individual request.
[04:38] Jon Park: yes small tradeoff: batching adds a small queuing delay but reduces tail and cost. for embeddings we target batching thresholds that keep median latency nearly the same while improving p95.
[04:49] Priya Rao: any quantification? numbers help with product decisions.
[04:53] Ava Martinez: we'll send token heatmaps and expected p95 improvements per recommendation — that's in the next steps.
[04:59] Sofia Alvarez: also want to call out monitoring — currently our observability only reports avg latency, not token-level or per-route cost. can we get better dashboards?
[05:08] Jon Park: yes redwood console supports token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards. we'll share a pre-built dashboard for your routes and a how-to to attach traces.
[05:18] Priya Rao: perfect. last product question — model versions. we want to pin generation model v1.3 for the recommender but use a cheaper quantized variant for background scoring. is that workable?
[05:29] Jon Park: absolutely. you can pin model versions per route and set fallback to quantized variants. runtime will handle kernel selection; we'll include recommended quantization profile for your workload.
[05:38] Ethan Cole: any known quality regressions when moving to q4_8 quantized models for background scoring?
[05:44] Jon Park: there can be small quality differences. Redwood Optimize can run a small eval against your prompt set to surface regressions — we'd recommend doing that on the scoring prompts before switching.
[05:54] Priya Rao: yes can you run that? we'll share the prompt set as an artifact.
[05:59] Ava Martinez: action — priya to share top-10 scoring prompts, jon to run the quantization eval.
[06:05] Kenji Ito: about cost reporting — can we get line items for embedding units as a separate row? our finance team needs a clean invoice mapping.
[06:14] Ava Martinez: finance mapping is doable; we'll export a sample billing CSV format and map the embedding vs gen lines.
[06:20] Sofia Alvarez: also retention — for logs and cached data what are retention defaults?
[06:24] Jon Park: defaults are 30 days for request logs in hosted but can be extended for Dedicated, and you can export to S3 with KMS. we will document the retention config.
[06:33] Priya Rao: great. schedule risk — we're planning a canary rollout for recommender to 20% of users next month; should we plan dedicated capacity before canary or rely on hosted?
[06:43] Jon Park: for a canary at 20% you can usually rely on hosted with autoscale and rate limits; if you expect user churn or heavy personalization calls then consider a small dedicated pool for the canary window.
[06:55] Ava Martinez: recap, we'll send the cost scenarios and token heatmap, jon will provide batching proxy example and run quantization eval once prompts are shared, security deep-dive next week, customer to run a staging soak/benchmark and post results.
[07:10] Priya Rao: all good. one last nit — earlier we saw one error code 503 with message 'model not ready' during a pod rotation. any quick mitigation?
[07:18] Jon Park: that's a cold-start issue during a scale down/in. mitigation: configure a short pre-warm duration or keep min replicas in the autoscale policy. we'll include suggested autoscale config.
[07:30] Ethan Cole: okay thanks.
[07:32] Ava Martinez: thanks everyone, i'll send notes and the attachments.
[07:36] Priya Rao: thanks ava.
[07:38] (meeting ends)

References & Links mentioned:
- Token heatmap & cost scenario (to be attached by Ava)
- Batching proxy example (to be attached by Jon)
- Prompt set (to be shared by Priya)
- Security docs (SOC2, KMS flows) — to be attached before the next call

End of transcript.
